acceleration.childMeaning: How quickly something's speed is changing.
practiceSentences: A sprinter's acceleration matters more than her top speed.
What causes the acceleration at the start of a race?
Acceleration is a change in speed, not speed itself.
The car's acceleration was measured over ten metres.
Slowing down is acceleration too, in the opposite direction.

acceptable.childMeaning: Good enough to be allowed or agreed to.
practiceSentences: A draw was an acceptable result away from home.
Is that an acceptable excuse for missing training?
An acceptable standard is a floor, not a target.
The referee ruled the boots acceptable.
What is acceptable in practice may not be in a match.

accommodate.childMeaning: To make room for someone, or to change a plan to suit them.
practiceSentences: The hall can accommodate the whole of Year 6 at once.
How many readers can this library accommodate?
She changed the timetable to accommodate the late bus.
A good plan can accommodate one surprise without collapsing.
Accommodate is spelled with two c's and two m's.

accommodation.childMeaning: A place for someone to stay or live.
practiceSentences: The school arranged accommodation for the visiting choir.
What accommodation is there near the coast?
Accommodation near the market costs more than it did.
Finding accommodation was harder than finding the money.
Accommodation carries the same double letters as accommodate.
Saving the deposit was an achievement in itself.
What achievement are you proudest of this year?
An achievement is measured against where you began.
The co-operative's greatest achievement was surviving its first year.
Achievement keeps the e of achieve before the ending.

acknowledgement.childMeaning: A statement accepting that something is true or has been received.
practiceSentences: The bank sent an acknowledgement of the payment.
Did you receive an acknowledgement of the order?
An acknowledgement is not the same as an agreement.
Her report opened with an acknowledgement of the help she had.
Acknowledgement keeps the e of acknowledge in British spelling.

adaptability.childMeaning: The ability to change to suit new conditions.
practiceSentences: Adaptability matters more than strength on a changing pitch.
What adaptability does a new sport demand?
Adaptability is a skill that can be practised.
The team's adaptability won them the second half.
Adaptability is not the same as having no plan.

adaptable.childMeaning: Able to change easily to suit a new situation.
practiceSentences: An adaptable player can cover two positions.
How adaptable is this training plan?
Adaptable equipment suits players of every size.
The coach wanted an adaptable squad, not eleven specialists.
Adaptable describes the person; adaptability is the quality.

adjacent.childMeaning: Next to or beside something else.
practiceSentences: The reserve is adjacent to the farmland.
Which habitat is adjacent to the wetland?
Two adjacent fields can hold quite different species.
Animals move between adjacent habitats through the corridor.
Adjacent means touching, or very nearly.

adjust.note: Meaning inherited and kept. Sentence 3 read 'A small adjustment early saves a large one later.' - `adjustment` is a derived noun, not the verb this card teaches. Same call as Grade 5's `profitable` on the `profit` card.
practiceSentences: Adjust the strap until the frame sits level.
What would you adjust first?
Adjust one thing at a time or you will not know what helped.
He adjusted the timing and the motor ran smoothly.
To adjust is to change a little; to redesign is to start again.

admittedly.childMeaning: Used to accept a point before making your own.
practiceSentences: Admittedly, the plan cost more than expected.
Is the ending, admittedly, a little sudden?
The tale is short; admittedly, it says a great deal.
Admittedly she was tired, but the work was finished.
Admittedly concedes something before the argument continues.

advantageous.childMeaning: Giving a benefit or putting you in a better position.
practiceSentences: Buying together proved advantageous for every stallholder.
Is an early payment advantageous to the seller?
An advantageous deal for one side is rarely lasting.
The position by the road was advantageous for trade.
Advantageous is the adjective of advantage.

agriculture.childMeaning: The growing of crops and the raising of animals for food.
practiceSentences: Agriculture depends on rain that arrives on time.
What share of the country works in agriculture?
Agriculture feeds a country before it earns for it.
New methods raised what agriculture could produce from one field.
Agriculture is farming, described from a distance.

allegory.childMeaning: A story whose characters and events stand for something larger.
practiceSentences: The fable is an allegory about greed.
What is this allegory really describing?
An allegory works on two levels at once.
Every character in the allegory stands for a kind of person.
An allegory says one thing and means another, on purpose.

alternative.note: Sentences 1 and 2 were the same sentence twice - 'When the bridge closed, the ferry became the only alternative for crossing the river.' beside 'When the lift broke, the stairs were the only alternative for reaching the library.' Identical frame, identical shape, one card. An exact-match check cannot see it and a word-overlap one cannot separate it from a card legitimately repeating its frame; reading it can.
practiceSentences: When the bridge closed, the ferry became the only alternative.
Can you suggest an alternative ending for the story we read today?
An alternative is worth having before you need it.
"Solar power is a clean alternative to burning coal," explained the visiting scientist.
Amara chose the alternative route home because the main road was flooded.

amateur.note: Meaning inherited and kept; it is accurate and within the cap.
practiceSentences: An amateur photographer took the best picture of the day.
Is this an amateur competition or a professional one?
Amal plays for an amateur team and trains twice a week.
An amateur does it for love; a professional does it for a living.
The word amateur comes from the Latin for `to love`.
She explained the heart using an analogy with a pump.
What analogy would make this idea clearer?
An analogy helps until it is pushed too far.
The teacher drew an analogy between a story and a journey.
A good analogy compares the unfamiliar with the familiar.

antibody.childMeaning: A protein the body makes to attack a particular germ.
practiceSentences: The body makes an antibody shaped to fit one germ.
How long does an antibody stay in the blood?
An antibody remembers a germ it has met before.
A vaccine teaches the body to make the antibody early.
Each antibody works on one invader and no other.

arguably.childMeaning: Used to say something can be argued, though others may disagree.
practiceSentences: This is arguably the finest fable in the collection.
Is the second ending arguably the stronger one?
Arguably, the villagers are more at fault than the boy.
The opening is arguably too slow for a short tale.
Arguably signals a claim you are prepared to defend.

attached.childMeaning: Joined or fixed to something, or fond of someone.
practiceSentences: A short note was attached to the parcel.
Which document is attached to this letter?
The shed is attached to the side of the house.
Dina grew very attached to the stray cat.
Attached keeps both t's when the ending is added.
The museum confirmed that the manuscript was authentic.
How can you tell whether this account is authentic?
An authentic voice is hard to imitate.
The story felt authentic because the details were exact.
Authentic means genuinely what it claims to be.

awareness.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Awareness means knowing about...' - restating its own headword.
practiceSentences: The campaign raised awareness of safe cycling.
What awareness does a goalkeeper need of the whole pitch?
Awareness of a risk is the first step to avoiding it.
Her awareness of the rules saved the team a penalty.
Awareness is noticing; action is what follows.

awkward.childMeaning: Uncomfortable or a little difficult, especially with other people.
awkward.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Awkward means uncomfortable...' - restating the headword the learner is already looking at.
practiceSentences: There was an awkward silence after the whistle.
Was the question awkward or simply unexpected?
She found the first training session awkward and the second easy.
An awkward tackle can injure both players.
Awkward is an awkward word to spell.
A balanced report gives both sides their strongest case.
Is this article balanced, or does it favour one view?
She wrote a balanced conclusion instead of a verdict.
A balanced argument is not the same as a weak one.
Amal kept her speech balanced even where she disagreed.

banking.childMeaning: The business of keeping, lending and moving people's money.
practiceSentences: Mobile banking reached the village before the road did.
How has banking changed in your grandparents' lifetime?
Banking runs on trust more than on buildings.
She works in banking and explains interest very clearly.
Banking lends out the money it is looking after.

bargain.childMeaning: Something bought cheaply, or an agreement about a price.
practiceSentences: The old bicycle was a real bargain.
Is that a bargain or just a low price?
They struck a bargain over the cost of the kit.
A bargain you never use has cost you everything.
Amara drove a hard bargain at the market.

belonging.childMeaning: The feeling of being accepted and welcome in a group.
belonging.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Belonging is the comfortable feeling...' - restating its own headword.
practiceSentences: A sense of belonging keeps players coming back.
What gives a new pupil a feeling of belonging?
Belonging comes from being needed, not just admitted.
She found a sense of belonging in the athletics club.
Belonging is built in small welcomes rather than one big one.

binary.childMeaning: A way of writing numbers using only 0 and 1.
practiceSentences: A computer stores everything as binary.
What is the number five in binary?
Binary uses two digits where we use ten.
Each binary digit is called a bit.
Binary is a choice between two states, on or off.

biodiversity.childMeaning: The range of different living things found in one place.
biodiversity.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning opened 'Biodiversity is the wide variety...' - restating the headword the learner is already looking at.
practiceSentences: The wetland has greater biodiversity than the farmland beside it.
Why does biodiversity matter to a forest's survival?
Biodiversity protects a habitat the way variety protects a diet.
Clearing one hedge lowered the biodiversity of the whole field.
Biodiversity counts kinds of life, not numbers of animals.

browser-based.childMeaning: Running inside a web browser rather than installed on the machine.
practiceSentences: The whole tool is browser-based, so nothing is installed.
Is this browser-based or does it need downloading?
A browser-based program updates for everyone at once.
Browser-based tools work on any machine with a browser.
Browser-based means the browser is doing the running.

bruise.childMeaning: A dark mark on the skin where it has been struck.
practiceSentences: A bruise appeared on his shin after the match.
How long does a bruise take to fade?
Ice reduces the swelling around a bruise.
A bruise is blood trapped under the skin.
Bruise rhymes with news, not with rise.

cache.childMeaning: A store of recently used data, kept close by so it can be fetched fast.
cache.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'A hidden store of things, often used to keep items safe' - the buried-treasure sense, on a card between networking and cursor. In computing a cache is not hidden and is not for safekeeping: it is a copy kept nearby for speed, which is the opposite emphasis.
practiceSentences: The browser keeps a cache so the page loads faster next time.
Why does clearing the cache sometimes fix a page?
A cache trades a little memory for a lot of speed.
A stale cache shows you yesterday's version of a page.
Cache is pronounced like cash, not like cachet.

catalyst.childMeaning: Something that speeds up a change without being used up itself.
practiceSentences: A catalyst speeds the reaction and survives it.
Which catalyst does this process need?
An enzyme is the body's own kind of catalyst.
Without a catalyst the change would take days.
A catalyst is also a person who makes something happen.

census.childMeaning: An official count of everybody living in a country.
practiceSentences: A census is taken once every ten years.
What does the census ask about?
A census plans the schools a district will need.
The census counted more people than anyone expected.
A census counts everyone; a sample counts a few.

chain.note: The inherited set opened with 'Water creates its own chain.', which explains nothing on its own, and closed with 'The next link in the chain is the herbivore...' - a sentence that begins mid-explanation with no previous link named. Both are the shape a sentence arrives in when it is mined from a passage.
practiceSentences: A food chain shows which living thing eats which.
Where does this chain begin?
Remove one species and the whole chain can fall apart.
Every food chain starts with a plant and ends with a decomposer.
Amara drew the chain from grass to zebra to lion.

chromosome.childMeaning: A thread inside a cell that carries the genes.
practiceSentences: Each chromosome carries hundreds of genes.
How many chromosomes does a human cell hold?
A chromosome is only visible when a cell divides.
Half of every chromosome pair comes from each parent.
Chromosome means coloured body, from the dye that first revealed it.

chronology.childMeaning: The order in which events actually happened.
practiceSentences: The chronology of the tale is not the order it is told in.
What chronology do these events really follow?
She drew a chronology of the whole year on one page.
A recount follows chronology; a mystery often does not.
Chronology and plot are two different things.

cloud-based.childMeaning: Stored and run on distant servers rather than on your own device.
practiceSentences: Their cloud-based storage keeps a copy off the premises.
Is a cloud-based system safer than a local one?
A cloud-based service works from any device you sign in on.
Cloud-based files survive a broken laptop.
Cloud-based means somebody else's computer, somewhere else.

coding.childMeaning: Writing the instructions that tell a computer what to do.
practiceSentences: Coding is a way of thinking before it is a way of typing.
What language did you start coding in?
Coding rewards somebody who enjoys being wrong quickly.
The club meets on Thursdays for coding.
Coding is the writing; the program is the result.

commence.childMeaning: To begin, especially something formal or planned.
practiceSentences: Building will commence once the drawings are approved.
When does the competition commence?
Work commenced before the materials arrived, which was a mistake.
The ceremony commenced at exactly nine o'clock.
Commence is the formal word; begin does the same work.
commence.note: The first meaning was 'To begin.' - true, and too short to teach anything; the card would have shown a learner two words.

commodity.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: Rice is a vital commodity that traders buy and sell in markets across the world.
Why does the price of a common commodity like wheat affect so many families?
"Clean water is the most precious commodity," the teacher reminded us during the lesson.
I learned that oil is a powerful commodity that shapes the economies of many nations.
A commodity is the same wherever it is sold, which is what sets its price.

comprehensive.childMeaning: Covering everything that is relevant, leaving nothing out.
practiceSentences: The report gave a comprehensive account of every cost.
Is this a comprehensive list or a selection?
A comprehensive answer takes longer and is worth it.
She made a comprehensive survey of every stall in the market.
Comprehensive means complete; comprehensible means understandable.

confidential.childMeaning: Meant to be kept private and shown only to certain people.
practiceSentences: The bank keeps every account confidential.
Which parts of this record are confidential?
Confidential information is lent, not given.
She marked the letter confidential before sending it.
Confidential means private by agreement, not merely secret.

contextualise.childMeaning: To place something in the setting that explains it.
practiceSentences: A short introduction will contextualise the letter.
How would you contextualise this fable for a younger reader?
To contextualise a fact is to say when and where it belongs.
She contextualised the quotation before analysing it.
A date and a place are often enough to contextualise a source.

contradictory.childMeaning: Saying the opposite of something else, so both cannot be true.
practiceSentences: The two witnesses gave contradictory accounts.
Why are these instructions contradictory?
Contradictory evidence means somebody is mistaken.
His actions were contradictory to everything he had said.
Two contradictory rules cannot both be followed.

controversy.childMeaning: A public disagreement in which people take strong opposite sides.
practiceSentences: The referee's decision caused a controversy that lasted weeks.
Why is there such controversy about the new rule?
A controversy is not settled by the loudest voice.
The controversy over the stadium divided the whole town.
Controversy needs two sides who both believe they are right.

coping.childMeaning: Dealing with something difficult without being overwhelmed.
practiceSentences: Coping with a loss takes longer than people expect.
What coping strategies help before a big match?
Coping is not the same as pretending nothing is wrong.
She has her own way of coping with a noisy house.
Asking for help is a form of coping, not a failure of it.

corporation.childMeaning: A large company that the law treats as a single body.
practiceSentences: The corporation employs people in nine countries.
Which corporation owns the factory now?
A corporation outlives the people who founded it.
A corporation can be sued in its own name.
A corporation is one company; a co-operative is many owners.

correspondingly.childMeaning: In a way that matches a change just described.
practiceSentences: The pitch was longer, and the match correspondingly slower.
Did the harder training bring a correspondingly better result?
Prices rose, and attendance fell correspondingly.
Correspondingly fewer injuries followed the new warm-up.
Correspondingly signals that two changes move together.

credible.childMeaning: Believable, because there is good reason to accept it.
credible.note: The inherited meaning was 'believable or trustworthy; something that can be trusted' - lowercase, no full stop, and circular, since it explains `trustworthy` with `can be trusted`.
practiceSentences: The witness gave a credible account of the evening.
Is that a credible explanation for the missing key?
A credible source names where its facts came from.
The excuse was not credible, and everyone knew it.
Credible means worth believing, not merely possible.

critique.childMeaning: A careful judgement of a piece of work, saying what does and does not succeed.
practiceSentences: Her critique of the poem was fair and detailed.
What critique would you offer the writer?
A critique is not an attack, and not praise either.
He wrote a short critique of the article for the newsletter.
A useful critique names one thing to change first.
Curiosity is what keeps a field biologist watching for hours.
What first stirred your curiosity about wild animals?
Curiosity killed the cat, but it also wrote every field guide.
Her curiosity about the nest cost her a whole afternoon.
Curiosity asks the question; patience answers it.

cursor.childMeaning: The mark on a screen showing where the next action will happen.
practiceSentences: The cursor blinks where the next letter will appear.
Where is the cursor now?
A cursor changes shape to say what a click will do.
She moved the cursor to the end of the line.
The cursor was named after a sliding part of a slide rule.

debugging.childMeaning: Finding and fixing the mistakes in a program.
practiceSentences: Debugging takes longer than writing the code did.
Where would you start debugging this?
Debugging is easier if you change one thing at a time.
She spent the whole afternoon debugging a single line.
The word debugging comes from a real moth in a real machine.

decomposer.childMeaning: A living thing that breaks down dead material.
practiceSentences: Fungi are the forest's most important decomposers.
What would happen without decomposers?
A decomposer returns nutrients to the soil.
Decomposers are the last link, and also the first.
Bacteria and fungi are the two great groups of decomposers.

deduce.childMeaning: To work something out from the evidence you already have.
practiceSentences: From the muddy footprints we can deduce which way he went.
What can you deduce from the opening paragraph?
A reader deduces the ending long before it arrives.
She deduced the answer without being told any of it.
To deduce is to reason, not to guess.

dependent.childMeaning: Relying on something or someone else.
practiceSentences: The harvest is dependent on the March rains.
Is the whole plan dependent on one supplier?
A town dependent on a single crop has no cushion.
She was financially dependent until the shop broke even.
Dependent with an e is the adjective; a dependant is a person.

devise.childMeaning: To think out and plan something new.
practiceSentences: They set out to devise a cheaper way to pump water.
How would you devise a test for this?
To devise is to invent the method, not just the idea.
She devised a system that needed no electricity.
Devise is the verb; a device is what it produces.

dialect.childMeaning: A form of a language spoken in one area or by one group.
dialect.note: The inherited meaning began lowercase and ended without a full stop - one of four in this grade's draft that arrive that way, with persistent (u2) and transition (u8).
practiceSentences: Every region of the coast has its own dialect.
Which dialect is spoken in your grandmother's town?
A dialect is a way of speaking, not a mistake.
The story is written in dialect, so read it aloud.
A dialect has its own words and its own grammar.

diction.childMeaning: A writer's or speaker's choice of words.
practiceSentences: The poet's diction is plain and very exact.
How would you describe the diction of this speech?
Diction changes the mood more than the plot does.
Formal diction suits a report and not a fable.
Amara noticed the diction shift the moment the elder spoke.

differentiate.childMeaning: To see or show the difference between two things.
practiceSentences: Can you differentiate a crocodile from an alligator?
How do you differentiate these two footprints?
Size alone will not differentiate the male from the female.
She learned to differentiate the calls by ear.
To differentiate is to name the difference, not just feel it.

diffusion.childMeaning: The spreading of a substance from where there is more to where there is less.
practiceSentences: Oxygen reaches the blood by diffusion.
How does diffusion move a scent across a room?
Diffusion needs no pump and no energy.
Diffusion stops when the amounts even out.
A drop of ink spreading through water is diffusion.

disastrous.childMeaning: Causing very great harm or damage.
practiceSentences: Clearing the forest had disastrous effects on the river.
Why was that season so disastrous for the herd?
A disastrous drought can empty a valley in months.
Introducing one new species proved disastrous for the rest.
Disastrous keeps the o of disaster and loses the e.

distribution.note: Sentences 2 and 4 were the same sentence twice - 'The fair distribution of food ensured every family at the harvest gathering was fed.' beside 'Fair distribution of food after the storm meant that every hungry family received an equal portion.' One frame, one card.
practiceSentences: Careful distribution meant that the last lorry of rice reached even the most distant village.
The fair distribution of food ensured every family at the gathering was fed.
Why does the uneven distribution of wealth cause problems in so many societies?
Distribution is as difficult as production, and is planned for less.
I helped organise the distribution of books so no classroom was left without any.

dynamic.childMeaning: Always changing or full of energy and movement.
practiceSentences: A river delta is a dynamic landscape.
How dynamic is this population from year to year?
A dynamic system settles into no single state.
The herd's dynamic movement follows the rain.
Dynamic is the opposite of static.

embryo.childMeaning: A living thing in the earliest stage of its development.
practiceSentences: The embryo grows from a single fertilised cell.
How long does the embryo stage last?
An embryo is protected inside the seed or the body.
The embryo of a bean sits between the two halves.
Every large animal began as an embryo too small to see.

enterprise.childMeaning: A business, or the willingness to start something difficult.
practiceSentences: The bakery began as a family enterprise.
What enterprise would you start with a small loan?
An enterprise needs a customer before it needs a logo.
Her enterprise in finding a supplier saved the shop.
Enterprise means the business, and also the nerve to begin it.

enzyme.childMeaning: A substance that speeds up a chemical change inside the body.
practiceSentences: An enzyme in saliva begins breaking down starch.
Which enzyme acts on protein in the stomach?
An enzyme speeds a reaction without being used up.
Enzymes stop working if they get too hot.
Each enzyme fits one job, like a key in a lock.

equipped.childMeaning: Supplied with what is needed for a task.
practiceSentences: The team arrived well equipped for a week in the bush.
Is the camp equipped for the rainy season?
A camel is equipped for heat in ways a horse is not.
They equipped every ranger with a radio.
Equipped doubles the p before the ending.

evidently.childMeaning: In a way that is clear from what can be seen.
practiceSentences: He was evidently exhausted by the final lap.
Is the ankle evidently swollen, or only sore?
Evidently the notice had never been read.
She had evidently practised the routine many times.
Evidently means the evidence shows it, not that somebody said so.

excretion.childMeaning: The removal of waste the body has produced.
practiceSentences: Excretion removes what the body cannot use.
Which organs are involved in excretion?
Excretion and digestion are not the same process.
Sweating is a form of excretion as well as cooling.
Without excretion, waste would build up and poison the body.

explicit.childMeaning: Stated openly and clearly, leaving nothing to be guessed.
practiceSentences: The instructions were explicit about the deadline.
Was the warning explicit or merely suggested?
An explicit rule saves an argument later.
She made her disagreement explicit rather than hinting.
Explicit is stated; implicit is understood.

export.childMeaning: To send goods to another country to be sold there.
practiceSentences: The country exports coffee and imports machinery.
What does this region export?
Exports earn the foreign money a country needs.
They began to export once the port was rebuilt.
An export leaves; an import arrives.

extraordinary.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: Dina's talent for weaving was truly extraordinary.
Isn't it extraordinary how quickly she finished the whole cloth?
What an extraordinary sunset this is tonight, Amal!
The scientist made an extraordinary discovery after years of study.
An extraordinary claim needs extraordinary evidence.
The plan is feasible if the parts arrive on time.
Is a solar version feasible for a village?
Feasible asks whether it CAN be done, not whether it should be.
They rejected two designs and kept the feasible one.
A feasible idea is one you could start on Monday.

fertilisation.childMeaning: The joining of a male and a female cell to begin new life.
practiceSentences: Fertilisation is the first step in reproduction.
Where does fertilisation take place in a flower?
After fertilisation the cell begins to divide.
Fertilisation in fish usually happens in the water.
Fertilisation also describes feeding soil for crops.

finance.childMeaning: The managing of money, or the money needed for something.
practiceSentences: The council could not find the finance for the bridge.
Who manages the finance for the co-operative?
Finance decides which good ideas actually happen.
She studied finance and returned to advise the village.
To finance something is to pay for it over time.

firmware.childMeaning: Software stored permanently inside a device.
practiceSentences: The printer's firmware controls how it feeds paper.
When was the firmware last updated?
Firmware sits between hardware and ordinary software.
A firmware update can add features to a device you already own.
Firmware is firm because it is not meant to change often.

foreshadowing.childMeaning: A hint early in a story about what will happen later.
practiceSentences: The storm on page one is foreshadowing.
Where does the foreshadowing begin?
Foreshadowing makes an ending feel earned rather than sudden.
You often notice the foreshadowing only on a second reading.
Good foreshadowing hints without giving anything away.

fragile.note: All five inherited sentences were about MONEY - family finances, a small business, savings, a buyer and a seller - in a unit about wildlife. Only the last mentioned the natural world at all. Rewritten to this unit; the money sentences belong to unit 5, which teaches its own words for that.
practiceSentences: A coral reef is beautiful and extremely fragile.
Why is this habitat so fragile after a dry season?
A fragile ecosystem recovers slowly, if it recovers at all.
The eggs are fragile, so the rangers move nobody near them.
Fragile does not mean unimportant; it means easily lost.

gene.childMeaning: A section of a chromosome that decides one inherited feature.
practiceSentences: A gene decides whether the seed grows tall or short.
Which gene controls the colour of the coat?
One gene can be carried without ever being shown.
Genes are passed on whole, not blended.
A gene is an instruction; the animal is the result.

generalise.childMeaning: To draw a wide conclusion from a small number of cases.
practiceSentences: It is unwise to generalise from one example.
Why do people generalise so quickly?
A fable invites you to generalise from one animal to many.
She refused to generalise about a whole town.
To generalise well you need more than two cases.

global.childMeaning: Affecting or covering the whole world.
practiceSentences: Migration routes are a global phenomenon.
What global change threatens this species?
A global problem needs more than a local answer.
The survey collected global data over ten years.
Global means worldwide, not merely widespread.
Tourists who harass an animal change how it behaves.
Why do smaller birds harass a hawk?
Do not harass a nesting bird for a photograph.
The rangers stop visitors who harass the elephants.
Harass has one r and two s's, which trips most people.
Henceforth the reserve will be closed to vehicles.
Will the rule apply henceforth, or from next year?
The species was henceforth protected by law.
Henceforth all sightings must be recorded on the same form.
Henceforth looks forward; hitherto looks back.

hindrance.note: Inherited whole and kept; the set is varied, inside the cap and about designing something, which is this unit.
practiceSentences: The rain was a hindrance to our outdoor game.
Bulky packaging is a real hindrance when families try to carry groceries home by bicycle.
Is a lack of recycling bins the biggest hindrance to sorting waste at school?
"My broken wrist was a hindrance," admitted Sami, "but the team adjusted the prototype schedule."
I thought rules would be a hindrance to creativity, yet limits actually sharpened our design.

hormone.childMeaning: A chemical messenger the body makes to control how it works.
practiceSentences: A hormone travels through the blood to reach its target.
Which hormone controls how tall a person grows?
Hormones work slowly compared with nerve signals.
One hormone can affect several parts of the body at once.
The class labelled where each hormone is made.

imply.childMeaning: To suggest something without saying it directly.
practiceSentences: Her tone seemed to imply that she disagreed.
What does the last line imply about the ending?
A writer may imply far more than the words say.
Do not imply what you are willing to state.
To imply is the writer's side; to infer is the reader's.

import.childMeaning: To bring goods in from another country to sell.
practiceSentences: They import rice when the harvest is poor.
What does the town import that it once made itself?
Imports fill a gap the country cannot fill itself.
A tax on imports protects local makers and raises prices.
Import in and export out, which is how to remember them.

inasmuch.childMeaning: To the extent that; because of the fact that.
practiceSentences: The plan succeeded inasmuch as the herd survived.
Is it a success inasmuch as anything was saved?
Inasmuch as the rains failed, the count was always going to fall.
She agreed, inasmuch as the evidence allowed.
Inasmuch is followed by `as`, and always has been.
The second model incorporates the solar panel.
How could we incorporate both suggestions?
To incorporate is to build in, not to attach on.
She incorporated the feedback into the next drawing.
A good design incorporates its limits rather than fighting them.

infrastructure.childMeaning: The roads, power and water a country needs to work.
practiceSentences: No business grows without infrastructure to reach it.
What infrastructure does this district still lack?
Infrastructure costs a great deal and is noticed only when it fails.
The port is the most valuable infrastructure on the coast.
Infrastructure is what everything else is built on top of.

inheritance.childMeaning: The passing of features from parents to their young.
practiceSentences: Eye colour is decided by inheritance.
What features come to a cub through inheritance?
Inheritance explains why offspring resemble their parents.
Inheritance passes on the instructions, not the experiences.
Inheritance also means property left to somebody.

innovative.childMeaning: New in a way that improves on what came before.
practiceSentences: The cooling design was genuinely innovative.
What makes an idea innovative rather than merely new?
An innovative solution often looks obvious afterwards.
Their innovative use of clay kept the water cold.
Innovative means it works AND it is new; new alone is not enough.
The model works insofar as the wind stays light.
Is the test useful insofar as it copies real conditions?
Insofar as we could measure, the two performed the same.
She agreed insofar as the cost allowed.
Insofar is followed by `as`, always.

insufficient.childMeaning: Not as much as is needed.
practiceSentences: Insufficient sleep slows every kind of recovery.
Was the warm-up insufficient for such a cold day?
Insufficient evidence is not the same as evidence against.
One bottle of water proved insufficient for the whole team.
Insufficient means short of enough, not close to nothing.

intensive.childMeaning: Involving a great deal of effort in a short time.
practiceSentences: The squad began an intensive week of training.
Is intensive practice better than steady practice?
An intensive course covers a term in a fortnight.
Intensive training without rest causes injury.
Intensive means concentrated, not merely long.
Most animals on Earth are invertebrates.
Which invertebrate is the largest?
An invertebrate may still have a hard outer shell.
Worms, insects and jellyfish are all invertebrates.
Invertebrate simply means not a vertebrate.

kinetic.childMeaning: To do with movement, or the energy a moving thing has.
practiceSentences: A moving ball carries kinetic energy.
How much kinetic energy does a runner have?
Kinetic energy grows quickly as speed increases.
A stretched bow stores energy and releases it as kinetic.
Kinetic comes from the Greek word for motion.

larva.childMeaning: The young form of an insect, quite unlike the adult.
practiceSentences: The larva looks nothing like the moth it becomes.
What does this larva eat before it pupates?
A larva must moult before it can grow further.
Mosquito larvae live in still water.
The plural of larva is larvae, not larvas.

leisure.childMeaning: Time when you are free to do as you please.
practiceSentences: Many inventions were built in somebody's leisure hours.
What do you do with your leisure time?
Leisure is not the same as doing nothing.
The workshop is open for leisure use at weekends.
Leisure rhymes with pleasure, and is spelled nothing like it sounds.

likelihood.childMeaning: How probable it is that something will happen.
practiceSentences: The likelihood of rain in March is high.
What is the likelihood of the price falling again?
Likelihood is a judgement, and probability is its number.
They weighed the likelihood of a poor harvest before borrowing.
A small likelihood is not the same as none.

manipulate.childMeaning: To handle or work something skilfully, especially with the hands or with data.
manipulate.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'To control or influence someone unfairly, often through trickery' - the SOCIAL sense, which is real and belongs beside persuasion rather than beside devise, refine and troubleshoot. In a unit about designing and building, to manipulate is what a robot arm and a spreadsheet do. The unfair sense is named in the fifth sentence rather than dropped.
practiceSentences: The robot arm can manipulate objects too small for fingers.
How does the program manipulate the data?
Long tongs let you manipulate something far too hot to touch.
She manipulated the figures into a chart in one step.
Manipulate can also mean to control a person unfairly, which is a different thing entirely.

manufacture.childMeaning: To make goods in large amounts, usually with machines.
practiceSentences: The plant manufactures roofing sheets.
What do they manufacture here?
To manufacture is to make many, not to make one.
Manufacturing moved to where the power was cheapest.
Manufacture also means to invent an excuse.

microorganism.childMeaning: A living thing too small to see without a microscope.
practiceSentences: A single spoonful of soil holds millions of microorganisms.
Which microorganisms break down fallen leaves?
Not every microorganism causes disease.
Microorganisms were unknown until the lens was invented.
A microorganism can be a bacterium, a fungus or an alga.

mode.childMeaning: The value that appears most often in a set of numbers.
practiceSentences: The mode is the price that came up most often.
What is the mode of these market takings?
A set can have two modes, or none at all.
The mode is the only average that works for words as well as numbers.
Mode also means a way of doing something.

monitor.childMeaning: To watch something carefully over a period of time.
monitor.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning joined two senses - 'A screen that shows information; to watch something carefully' - and three of its four sentences were about the screen. In this unit `monitor` sits with quantify, differentiate and scrutinise, where it is what a scientist does to a population. The screen sense is named in the fifth sentence.
practiceSentences: Rangers monitor the herd throughout the dry season.
How often should we monitor the water level?
To monitor is to watch over time, not to glance once.
Amal monitors the nest from a distance so the birds settle.
A monitor is also the screen the readings appear on.

monologue.childMeaning: A long speech by one person, spoken alone or to others.
practiceSentences: The play opens with a monologue.
How long should a monologue be?
A monologue lets us hear a character think.
Dina wrote a monologue for the fox in the fable.
A monologue has one voice; a dialogue has two.

motif.childMeaning: An image or idea that returns again and again in a story.
practiceSentences: Water is the central motif of the whole collection.
Which motif appears in every chapter?
A motif gathers meaning each time it returns.
The broken clock is a motif, not a coincidence.
Amara traced one motif through all four fables.

networking.childMeaning: Connecting computers so they can share information.
practiceSentences: Networking lets one printer serve a whole room.
What networking does the school building need?
Networking turns many machines into one shared resource.
A networking fault can look exactly like a broken program.
Networking also means building useful contacts among people.

nucleus.childMeaning: The control centre of a cell, holding its chromosomes.
practiceSentences: The nucleus holds the instructions for the whole cell.
Which part of the cell is the nucleus?
A cell without a nucleus cannot divide normally.
The nucleus is separated from the rest by a membrane.
Nucleus also names the centre of an atom.

nuisance.childMeaning: Something or someone that causes trouble or annoyance.
practiceSentences: A loose cable is a nuisance and a danger.
Is the noise a nuisance or just a distraction?
The old printer was more nuisance than help.
She fixed the nuisance rather than working around it.
Nuisance ends in -ance, not -ence.

nutrient.childMeaning: A substance in food that the body needs to live and grow.
practiceSentences: Beans are a good source of every main nutrient.
Which nutrient does the body use for building muscle?
A nutrient the body cannot make must come from food.
Cooking for too long destroys some of the nutrients.
Water carries nutrients to every cell.

operating.childMeaning: Running or controlling something, as an operating system runs a computer.
practiceSentences: The operating system starts before anything else does.
Which operating system does this machine use?
An operating system shares the processor between programs.
She was operating the machine when it stopped.
An operating system is the program every other program stands on.

ownership.note: Sentence 3 named Omar, Grade 3's shopkeeper, who is not in this grade's readings - and the set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: Under the old system, ownership of the land belonged to just a few families.
Does shared ownership of the fields really make life fairer for everyone?
Would you give up ownership of a stall for the community's sake?
The new policy promised a fairer kind of ownership across the whole village.
Ownership carries responsibility as well as rights.

peripheral.childMeaning: A device connected to a computer to add to what it can do.
practiceSentences: A mouse is a peripheral, not part of the computer itself.
Which peripheral would help most here?
A peripheral can be added or removed without opening the case.
The scanner is the only peripheral the room shares.
Peripheral also means at the edge, and that is the same idea.

persistent.childMeaning: Continuing steadily even when it is difficult.
persistent.note: The inherited meaning began lowercase and ended without a full stop - one of the four in this grade's draft that arrive that way.
practiceSentences: A persistent cough should be shown to a doctor.
Was she persistent or simply stubborn?
Persistent effort beats occasional brilliance.
The persistent rain cancelled every fixture.
Persistent means it keeps going, whether you want it to or not.

photosynthetic.childMeaning: Able to make food from sunlight, water and air.
practiceSentences: Photosynthetic plants sit at the base of every food chain.
Which photosynthetic organisms live in the sea?
A photosynthetic cell contains chlorophyll.
Some bacteria are photosynthetic as well as plants.
Photosynthetic describes the organism; photosynthesis is what it does.

potential.note: Sentence 1 named Teacher Yasmin, who belongs to Grade 5 - and the set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: Every pupil in the class was said to have great potential.
Does the new farming programme really have the potential to help everyone?
Sami, this idea has real potential if the council would only listen!
Amal's essay explored the potential of shared fields to reduce hunger.
Potential is what could happen, and it is not a promise.

presumably.childMeaning: Probably, judging by what is known.
practiceSentences: The battery is flat, so presumably it was left switched on.
Is the second version presumably the better one?
Presumably nobody tested it in the rain.
She had presumably read the instructions already.
Presumably signals a reasonable guess, not a fact.

production.note: Sentence 5 read 'Its production of clean water must support all the nearby communities.' - an `its` with no referent anywhere on the card, the shape a sentence takes when it is lifted from a passage.
practiceSentences: The factory improved its production by introducing a faster, smarter assembly line.
How long does the production of a single handmade instrument usually take?
"Our play's production begins next week," the drama teacher announced excitedly.
I helped with the production of the school magazine by designing its bright cover.
Production counts what is made; productivity counts how efficiently.

protagonist.repitchedFrom: grade 5 unit 4: 'The main character, whose story the reader follows.' - correct, and this grade inherited it word for word with all five sentences, so a learner who completed Grade 5 would meet an identical card. Repitched to what Grade 6 adds: the protagonist as the character who WANTS something and is changed by pursuing it, which is what makes plot rather than sequence.
protagonist.childMeaning: The character whose wanting drives the story and who is changed by it.
practiceSentences: A protagonist is not simply the person on every page.
What does the protagonist of this fable actually want?
The protagonist ends the story as somebody slightly different.
Amal argued that the village, not the boy, is the real protagonist.
A story can have a protagonist you do not like at all.

protocol.childMeaning: An agreed set of rules for how two machines exchange information.
protocol.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'The official set of steps or rules for doing something correctly' - the general procedural sense, and all five sentences were about a market inspection and a food stall. On a card sitting between networking and firmware, protocol is what lets two machines agree. Two of the sentences were faulty besides: one named Theo, who belongs to Grades 2 and 3, and read 'Theo, he completely ignored the protocol!'; another, 'The officer's observation lacked protocol.', is not a use of the word.
practiceSentences: Two machines can only talk if they share a protocol.
Which protocol does this connection use?
A protocol settles the order and the format in advance.
The web runs on a protocol agreed decades ago.
A protocol is also the correct way to behave on a formal occasion.

puberty.childMeaning: The stage when a child's body develops into an adult's.
practiceSentences: Puberty begins at different ages for different people.
What changes happen to the body during puberty?
Puberty is driven by hormones released inside the body.
There is no single right age for puberty to start.
Puberty takes several years, not a single moment.

quantify.childMeaning: To measure something and express it as a number.
practiceSentences: It is hard to quantify the damage after one season.
How would you quantify the size of this population?
To quantify a change you need a measurement from before.
They quantified the loss in hectares rather than in words.
Some things matter and cannot be quantified.
A printer holds each job in a queue.
How long is the queue for the workshop?
A queue is served in the order it was joined.
Tasks wait in a queue until the processor is free.
Queue is one letter followed by four that say nothing.
Each version of the prototype refined the last.
What would you refine before showing it to anyone?
To refine is to improve by small steps, not to start again.
They refined the design over eleven attempts.
Refining is where most of the invention actually happens.
Transport here is relatively cheap.
Is the fee relatively high for this district?
Relatively few families own the land they farm.
The scheme was relatively simple to run.
Relatively always leaves a question: compared with what?

reproduction.childMeaning: The process by which living things produce young.
practiceSentences: Reproduction is one of the signs of a living thing.
How does reproduction differ between plants and animals?
Reproduction passes characteristics from parent to offspring.
Some plants manage reproduction without any seeds.
Reproduction also means making a copy of a picture.

resistance.childMeaning: A force that slows something down as it moves through air or water.
resistance.repitchedFrom: the inherited meaning was 'The act of standing firm against something, such as unfair rules or control.' - the POLITICAL sense, on a card sitting beside acceleration, kinetic and transfer. In a unit about sport and the body, resistance is the force a swimmer and a cyclist work against.
practiceSentences: A swimmer's cap reduces resistance in the water.
How does a cyclist lower air resistance?
Resistance grows as a moving object goes faster.
The parachute works by creating as much resistance as possible.
Resistance in a wire turns electrical energy into heat.

robotics.childMeaning: The design and building of machines that can act on their own.
practiceSentences: Robotics brings together coding, electronics and engineering.
What can robotics do that a person cannot?
Robotics needs a sensor as much as it needs a motor.
The robotics club built an arm that sorts by colour.
Robotics is a field; a robot is one thing in it.

sacrifice.note: The inherited set held four sentences, not five.
practiceSentences: The volunteers made a real sacrifice, giving up their weekends to rebuild the flooded school.
What sacrifice would you make to help a cause you truly believe in?
"Every great change requires sacrifice," the teacher reminded the determined young activists.
I understood the meaning of sacrifice when my parents worked extra hours for my education.
A sacrifice costs the person making it, or it is not one.

sample.note: The inherited set held ONE sentence - 'One sample glowed faintly blue.' - which explains nothing standing alone and belongs to an experiment the card never shows.
practiceSentences: A sample is a small part chosen to stand for the whole.
How large a sample would you need to trust the result?
A sample chosen carelessly tells you about nobody.
They tested a sample of grain from every sack.
A census counts everyone; a sample counts a few and reasons from them.

scrutinise.childMeaning: To examine something very closely and carefully.
practiceSentences: Scrutinise the photograph before naming the species.
Why scrutinise a result you already expected?
A scientist must scrutinise the method as well as the answer.
They scrutinised every entry in the field notebook.
To scrutinise is to look harder than seems necessary.

sector.childMeaning: One part of a country's economy or activity.
practiceSentences: The farming sector employs most people here.
Which sector is growing fastest?
A country that depends on one sector is fragile.
The public sector is paid for out of taxation.
Sector also means a part of a circle.

sediment.childMeaning: Material that settles at the bottom of a liquid.
practiceSentences: Sediment settles where the river slows down.
What sediment did the flood leave behind?
Layers of sediment record thousands of years.
Sediment buries the remains that later become fossils.
Stir the bottle and the sediment lifts again.

self-awareness.childMeaning: Understanding your own feelings, strengths and limits.
practiceSentences: Self-awareness helps an athlete know when to rest.
How would you describe your own self-awareness?
Self-awareness means noticing a mood before it becomes a mistake.
Dina showed self-awareness by admitting she had rushed.
Self-awareness is harder than being aware of everybody else.

self-discipline.childMeaning: Making yourself do what you planned, even when you would rather not.
practiceSentences: Training every morning takes real self-discipline.
Where does self-discipline come from?
Self-discipline is a habit long before it is a feeling.
Amal's self-discipline showed in her steady improvement.
Self-discipline is choosing later over now.

simulation.childMeaning: A model that copies how something real behaves, so it can be studied.
practiceSentences: A simulation lets you crash the bridge without building it.
How accurate is this simulation?
A simulation is only as good as what was put into it.
Pilots train on a simulation before they fly.
A simulation predicts; it does not prove.

sincere.note: Sentence 1 named Teacher Yasmin, who belongs to Grade 5 and is not in this grade's readings.
practiceSentences: The quiet paper was the most sincere one in the pile.
A sincere apology comes from the heart.
Was his thank-you sincere and true?
Grandma said, "A sincere friend tells you the truth."
I wrote a sincere note to thank my teacher.

solvent.childMeaning: A liquid that dissolves another substance.
practiceSentences: Water is the solvent in almost every living cell.
Which solvent will dissolve this stain?
A solvent does the dissolving; the solute is dissolved.
Warming the solvent makes it work faster.
Water is called the universal solvent for good reason.

substantial.note: Sentence 5 was 'But something inside her - small but substantial - told her to speak.' Lifted from a narrative: it opens with `But`, names a `her` the card never introduces, and uses the word figuratively where the other four use it of amounts.
practiceSentences: The library received a substantial donation that funded meals for many needy families.
How long would it take to save such a substantial amount from weekly pocket money?
"That's a substantial saving," Sami noted, "if we buy in bulk and share the cost."
I put a substantial part of my earnings aside before spending anything on myself.
Substantial means large enough to matter, not merely large.

subtle.childMeaning: Slight and not obvious, but there if you look carefully.
practiceSentences: There is a subtle difference between the two endings.
Was the change subtle enough to miss?
A subtle hint is easily overlooked on a first reading.
The fable makes its point in a subtle way.
Subtle is spelled with a b nobody says.

sustainable.childMeaning: Able to continue for a long time without using everything up.
practiceSentences: Sustainable fishing leaves enough behind to breed.
Is this way of farming sustainable?
A sustainable harvest takes the interest, not the capital.
The reserve was designed to be sustainable for a century.
Sustainable asks what happens in fifty years, not next season.
Taxation pays for the roads and the clinics.
Is taxation fairer when the richest pay a larger share?
Taxation takes from everyone and spends on everyone.
The council explained where the taxation went.
Taxation is the system; a tax is one charge within it.

technical.childMeaning: To do with the practical details of how something works.
practiceSentences: The technical drawing shows every measurement.
What technical problem stopped the first model?
A technical explanation is not the same as a clear one.
She read the technical manual twice before starting.
Technical detail belongs in an appendix, not an introduction.

theoretically.childMeaning: According to the idea, though perhaps not in practice.
practiceSentences: Theoretically the fund is open to everyone.
Is that theoretically possible or actually possible?
Theoretically the two routes cost the same.
The scheme theoretically pays for itself within a year.
Theoretically signals that reality has not been consulted yet.

tourism.note: Inherited whole and kept - varied, inside the cap, and about this unit's subject.
practiceSentences: Tourism brings buses full of visitors to our seaside town.
Tourism gives many families in our town their jobs.
How does tourism help protect the old fort?
"Tourism grows when we keep our beaches clean," said the mayor.
My uncle works in tourism, guiding visitors around the city.
You can trace the motif back to the opening page.
Can you trace this saying to its original teller?
Historians trace the custom to a single village.
She traced the argument through every paragraph.
Trace the idea backwards and you find its source.

transfer.childMeaning: To move something from one place, person or form to another.
practiceSentences: Energy transfers from the muscles to the ball.
How does heat transfer through a metal spoon?
The player asked for a transfer to another club.
Transfer the reading into the table before you leave.
Energy is never lost, only transferred.

troubleshoot.childMeaning: To find out what is going wrong and put it right.
practiceSentences: Troubleshoot the power supply before blaming the software.
How would you troubleshoot a machine that will not start?
To troubleshoot is to work from the simplest cause upwards.
She troubleshoots by removing one part at a time.
Troubleshooting is a method, not a talent.

utilise.childMeaning: To make practical use of something.
practiceSentences: The design utilises heat that would otherwise be wasted.
What materials could we utilise instead?
To utilise is to put to use, often something already there.
They utilised old bicycle parts in the frame.
Utilise usually means use, and use is usually the better word.
A frog is a vertebrate and a beetle is not.
Which vertebrates live in this river?
Every vertebrate has an internal skeleton.
Fish were the first vertebrates to appear.
Vertebrates are a small share of all animal species.

vitamin.childMeaning: A nutrient the body needs in small amounts to stay healthy.
practiceSentences: Oranges are rich in vitamin C.
Which vitamin does sunlight help the body make?
A vitamin is needed in tiny amounts, but needed all the same.
Vitamins are lost when vegetables are boiled too long.
No single vitamin can replace a varied diet.
A tired player is vulnerable to injury.
Who is most vulnerable in very hot weather?
An unguarded goal is vulnerable from any angle.
She admitted feeling vulnerable before her first race.
Being vulnerable is a condition, not a weakness.
